lookForward.fits: The Richmond Park deer rut runs through late September and October; the Royal Parks ask visitors to keep 50 metres away.
lookForward.headline: The stags are roaring in Richmond Park
lookForward.line: It is the autumn rut: six hundred red and fallow deer live in the park, and the stags bellow and clash antlers at dawn and dusk. Richmond station, then a walk up the hill. Go early, keep fifty metres back, no dogs.

source.name: The Royal Parks: Deer in Richmond Park

more: Richmond Park in south-west London is the largest of the royal parks, about ten square kilometres of grass, bracken and old oaks, and some 600 red and fallow deer have lived there since the 1600s. Every autumn the red stags fight for the right to mate: they roar, they parade, and now and then two of them lock antlers and shove. The sound carries across the whole park.

Getting there: Richmond station on the District line and the Overground, then a twenty-minute walk up Richmond Hill to Richmond Gate. The pedestrian gates are open all day. The deer are often around Pen Ponds in the middle of the park, or anywhere among the bracken. Early morning is best, both for the stags and for having the place nearly to yourself.

The rules matter this month. Stay at least fifty metres from any deer, do not get between a stag and his hinds, and keep dogs on a lead or, better, at home. A stag in the rut is unafraid of people and does not stop to think.
